name: Italian (Min)

rules.name: Preparing for the Minor
rules.desc:
Highly Encouraged
To enroll in all Italian literature courses taught in Italian, students must pass first-year Italian [ITALLANG 1, 2, 3 or ITALLANG 1A, 2A] or complete the placement exam.
rules.notes: Students may contribute up to 12 units in second-year language courses to their Italian minor in the electives section.

rules.name: Required Courses
rules.desc:
Total unit count must reach at least 8 units.
To enroll in all Italian literature courses taught in Italian, students must pass first-year Italian [ITALLANG 1, 2, 3 or ITALLANG 1A, 2A] or complete the placement exam.

rules.name: Electives
rules.desc:
• Coursework within the department. Additional ITALIAN courses taught by Italian faculty (may be taught in English or Italian) at the 100- or 200-level.

• Coursework in other departments relevant to the degree, on Italian topics, with the approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Bing Overseas Study Program. Courses taken at the Bing Overseas Study Program in Florence with prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Education as Self-Fashioning (ESF). ESF courses taught at least partially by a French and Italian Department faculty member. Students may count a maximum of ten units.

• Structured Liberal Education. Students may count ten units of SLE coursework towards their major elective totals.

• Digital Humanities Course. Student work must reflect Italian interests. Prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies. Maximum of five units.

rules.notes: The remaining units toward the 24 unit total required for the minor will comprise elective courses. Prior approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies for elective courses is required.

gpa: A grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 or better must be achieved in each course.
grading: All courses applied to the Italian Culture and Literature subplans must be taken for a letter grade and passed with at least a ‘C’.
reviewNotes: You choose the Italian Culture or Italian Literature subplan. The audit checks the 24 units, the subplan's two required courses (at least 8 units), and up to 12 units of second-year Italian language courses (ITALLANG 21-23, 21A, 22A), all letter graded with a C or better. The rest are electives the Director of Undergraduate Studies approves in advance, which you move in by hand: ITALIAN courses at the 100 or 200 level, courses on Italian topics in other departments, Bing Overseas Florence, ESF (up to 10 units), SLE (up to 10 units) and Digital Humanities (up to 5 units). AP credit is not accepted.
